Read Today's Paper Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore SECTIONS Muthoot Finance Q2 cons profit jumps 36% YoY to Rs 3,278 crore By Atmadip Ray , ET Bureau Last Updated: Oct 31, 2026, 06:15:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 3,278 crore in Q2, while assets under management grew 42% to Rs 2.09 lakh crore. However, standalone gross NPA ratio rose to 3.87% from 2.28% in the previous quarter, indicating a deterioration in asset quality Reuters For 9 months, profit after tax surged 91% year-on-year to Rs 7,048 crore, compared with Rs 3,693 crore in the corresponding period last year. Kolkata: India's largest gold loan company Muthoot Finance reported a 36% year-on-year surge in consolidated net profit for the second quarter at Rs 3,278 crore, backed by 42% expansion in business while asset quality deteriorated. The net profit was Rs 2,412 crore in the year ago period. On a standalone basis, the company's second quarter net profit stood at Rs 2977 crore, up 27% over Rs 2345 in the year-ago quarter. Muthoot's consolidated assets under management grew 42% year-on-year to Rs 2.09 lakh crore at the end of September. Out of this, the gold loan stood at Rs 1.93 lakh crore. Its standalone AUM grew at the same pace to Rs 1.88 lakh crore, of which gold loan was Rs 1.79 lakh crore. Live Events The company's standalone gross non-performing assets ratio jumped to 3.87% at the end of September from 2.28% three months prior. Muthoot's subsidiary Belstar Microfinance earned a Rs 78 crore net profit for the quarter under review, widening from Rs 66 crore in the first quarter. Its asset quality improved with gross NPA ratio falling to 3.26% from 4.58% a year back. Its first half net profit stood at Rs 144 crore compared to a loss of Rs 160 crore in the year-ago six month. Its AUM stood at Rs 7,876 crore at the end of September against Rs 7,715 crore a year prior as industry-wide stress moderated disbursement growth, the company said. ETMarkets.com Nifty IT ’s 18% October surge may be more than an oversold rebound, with improving momentum, a bullish RSI crossover and a reclaim of key moving averages pointing to a possible leadership shift in favour of Indian technology stocks , according to Vatsal Bhuva, technical analyst at LKP Securities . He expects the index to target 35,000 as global profit-booking in AI and semiconductor stocks drives capital rotation towards Indian IT. Edited excerpts from a chat: Nifty gained around 2% in October, but the Nifty 500, midcaps and smallcaps have remained under pressure. Is this a genuine market recovery or merely a narrow largecap-led bounce? The divergence in market performance suggests that the ongoing recovery remains selective and largely driven by heavyweight large-cap stocks, rather than signalling a broad-based market turnaround. The October recovery was largely driven by a handful of heavyweight large-cap stocks rather than broad-based market participation. Nifty gained 1.91% during the month, whereas the Nifty Midcap 150 and Nifty Smallcap 100 indices declined 3.75% and 4.06%, respectively. Stocks from sectors such as IT, pharmaceuticals and banking contributed significantly to the Nifty's outperformance, particularly during the last week of October. This was also supported by the global rotation away from AI and semiconductor stocks amid profit booking. Live Events Going ahead, continued profit booking in global AI-related stocks could potentially benefit Indian IT companies. However, the divergence in market performance suggests that this is still a selective, largecap-led recovery rather than a broad-based market turnaround. There will be no fresh mainboard IPO launches, although several companies that raised funds in late October are preparing for their stock market debuts. Vedant Poly Fabs, a small and medium enterprise (SME), will be the only new company opening its IPO next week. Meanwhile, six companies whose public issues are currently open, including mainboard player Bombay Coated & Special Steels, are scheduled to list on the exchanges during the week. The slowdown follows a busy October for India's primary market, highlighted by Jio Platforms ' Rs 30,188 crore IPO, the largest in the country's history. Mukesh Ambani-led Jio made its stock market debut on October 28 at Rs 1,358, a premium of 21.36% over its issue price of Rs 1,119. The blockbuster offering attracted bids worth Rs 4.9 lakh crore in the public book and was subscribed more than 22 times. The coming week will see investors turn their attention towards the final subscription days of existing issues and the listing performance of recently concluded offerings. Retail investors will have to apply for a minimum of 2,400 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 2,25,600 at the upper end of the price band. The company is expected to finalise the basis of allotment on November 5, with its tentative listing on the NSE SME platform scheduled for November 9. Read Today's Paper Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty SECTIONS Sebi bars EKI Energy, MD Dabkara, others from market; imposes penalty PTI Last Updated: Nov 01, 2026, 09:23:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has taken serious action against EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director due to financial misreporting. The regulatory body discovered that the company recognized revenue too early and inflated expenses, distorting profit reports. In addition to the company's penalties totaling Rs 88 lakh, several executives were also fined for their complicity in these discrepancies. Agencies Markets regulator Sebi has barred EKI Energy Services Ltd and its Managing Director Manish Kumar Dabkara from the securities market for two months and 12 months, respectively, for misrepresenting financial statements of the carbon credits trading firm and diverting funds. Also, the regulator has restrained the company's former Chief Financial Officer (CFO) Mohit Kumar Agarwal from the securities market for eight months, while whole-time directors Naveen Sharma and Sonali Sheikh have been prohibited for five months and one month, respectively. Besides, Sebi has imposed monetary penalties totalling Rs 88 lakh on the company and other individuals for various violations of securities market regulations. Further, the markets regulator directed Dabkara to take immediate steps to recoup the amount diverted from EKI Energy Services. In its 94-page final order, Sebi noted that EKI had prematurely recognised revenue aggregating Rs 197.04 crore during the first three quarters of FY23, thereby misrepresenting its financial performance to investors. Live Events The regulator observed that "EKI's publication and continued disclosure of prematurely recognised revenue of Rs 197.04 crore constituted reckless financial misrepresentation connected with investor decisions concerning its listed shares". Also, the regulator found that EKI had overstated expenses by Rs 26.34 crore during FY22 and FY23, resulting in an understatement of its profits. "The company diverted Rs 26.34 crore by overstating expenses during 2021-22 and 2022-23," the order said. The regulator noted that EKI had "booked fictitious expenses against services not rendered", adding that payments made against such expenses "consequently constituted diversion of EKI's funds". Also, Sebi noted that Dabkara was responsible for the continued disclosure of misstated financial information and failure to ensure proper monitoring of the company's financial reporting systems. Also, the regulator held Sharma, Sheikh, and Agarwal liable for regulatory violations. Sebi imposed a penalty of Rs 12 lakh on EKI Energy Services, Rs 28 lakh on Dabkara, Rs 13 lakh on Sharma, Rs 6 lakh on Sheikh and Rs 19 lakh on Agarwal. Sebi also imposed monetary penalties on independent directors Ritesh Gupta and Burhanuddin Ali Husain Maksi Wala, besides former compliance officer Itisha Sahu.
